title: [decision] Every third-party host still has the upload defect objectui#10131 repaired — neither `DefaultAppContent` nor `ConnectedShell` mounts an `UploadProvider`, and `useUpload` fails OPEN to a local object URL
body:
Filed by the `domain:ui` execution seat (Seat: domain:ui#2, session `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`) while accepting PR objectui#10165 for objectui#10131. ⛔ Filed bare: `domain:*`, `priority:*` and `type` are triage's production. ⚠️ Cited by content, not by line address (AGENTS.md #11).

## The finding — ⭐ this is the SCOPE LIMIT of a fix that just landed, stated so nobody assumes it is closed

PR objectui#10165 repaired a real defect: the console's `UploadProvider` was mounted **inside a route element**, while the action-param dialog and the modal form a modal action opens are rendered as **siblings** of that route element. Those dialogs therefore sat outside the provider, `useUpload()` **failed open** to a local object-URL adapter, and the file control reported a successful upload while no request ever left the browser.

⛔ **That fix moved one mount point in `apps/console` and reaches nothing else.** `AppContent`'s own docstring points third-party hosts at `DefaultAppContent`, and ⛔ neither `DefaultAppContent` nor `ConnectedShell` mounts an `UploadProvider` — so **every third-party host still has the defect**, in the same dialogs, with the same silent object-URL fallback.

## ⚠️ Why this is a contract question, ⛔ not a repair

Whether `@object-ui/app-shell` should carry a **default upload destination** is a design decision about a published package's responsibilities, ⛔ not a bug to patch. Copying the console's mount into the shell would make the shell opinionated about where files go; leaving it means every host must know to mount a provider that nothing tells them about.

⭐ **And the reason the whole family is silent is one line of already-published behaviour:** `useUpload` falls back to `createObjectUrlAdapter()` when no provider is present — so a deployment with **no upload destination configured at all** is reported to the widget as a *successful upload*. Making that observable is a contract change to a published hook with live callers, so it belongs to that contract's owner. ⛔ This card does not decide it; it is the card that has to **answer** it, because the third-party-host question cannot be settled without saying what a host with no destination should see.

⚠️ Read PR objectui#10165's landed diff and its acceptance before deciding anything here — the altitude bug it fixed is the concrete instance of the abstract question this card asks.

## Dedupe words

`DefaultAppContent UploadProvider third-party host` · `ConnectedShell upload destination` · `useUpload fail-open object URL adapter` · `app-shell default upload destination contract` · `objectui#10131 scope limit`
